en: In the *Po-sa-wen* (Upoṣadha Text) and other such works, it is said that the various Buddhas manifest skillful means (*upāya-kauśalya*) to transform sentient beings; when the multitudes behold and revere them, their base delusions are extinguished.

Although the Dharma expounds the Three Vehicles and the precepts [differ], there are distinctions in their opening and closing according to the capacities of those who are dull or sharp. As for ordinary beings...
All who see or hear [this] shall receive supreme benefit;
such is the matter of this assembly. At that time, I, together with the *upādhyāya* and the *ācārya*, served as the masters who exhorted and guided [the practitioners].
This shall cause the true breeze to spread widely and the Buddha-sun to shine once more, providing an occasion for the officials and the common people to extend the merit of hearing the Dharma.
At that time, the ground of the Dharma was opened and the golden banner was erected.

The incense smoke and auspicious signs blend with the pure chanting and the resonance of the lute; the counting sticks proclaim liberation, and as one receives and upholds the name of the Precepts, one guards against wrongdoing. May the seeds of the Bodhi-treasury be moistened by the nectar of immortality.
Drawing from the auspicious flowers of the Tree of Fragrant Awakening,
they form the flavorful fruits of the Garden of Incense;
with each of these, they first provide adornment.
May Brahmā, Śakra, the various kings, the nāgas, devas, and the eight classes of beings,
through their bodily radiance, increase their holy power and silently protect all living beings;
may they uphold this teaching so that the Yin and Yang may accord with their proper order.
The sounds of wind and rain are harmonious;
the harvests are bountiful;
and the people delight in their occupations.
Furthermore, adorned with supreme merit and praised by the holy spirits,
I humbly pray that your longevity may equal that of the sacred rock and your life-span that of the numinous locust tree.
May the officials and functionaries diligently serve the boundless venerable elders;
may their merit support all sentient beings,
so that thereafter weapons and blades shall be forever abolished.
The traces of the teaching have been circulated;
may all sentient beings without exception ascend the path of enlightenment.
Regarding the *Poṣadha* Text: the Dharma King has manifested his response, his majesty shaking the great trichiliocosm.
It is our duty to cause the Dharma teachings to flourish and spread;
how much more so when proclaiming the treasury of the precepts?
By diligently observing them twice every month without transgression, one provides a foundation of merit for both family and state.
Thereupon, the banners and bells summoned the assembly, and the *brahmanic* music extended an invitation to the monks.
Fragrance rose in five clouds and the pennants shone with manifold colors;
all these manifold merits and boundless auspicious conditions were employed as adornments.
May the celestial immortals, dragons, spirits, and the eight classes of divine beings of the upper realms,
through their majestic spiritual power, provide secret protection and secretly bestow their sacred virtue,
so that the sun and moon may remain eternally bright and clear.
The sequence of Yin and Yang is regulated;
gentle breezes respond to the seasons,
and sweet rains follow their proper time.
May these four classes of people find joy in peace at the borders,
and may there be no cause for apprehension ten thousand *li* away for all eternity. Thus,
I pray that the Dharma may spread forever and the teachings of Śākyamuni be widely disseminated.
May all sentient beings together ascend the path of enlightenment.
Regarding the *Poṣadha* Text: I have observed that in the region of Liusha alone, there are several hundred monastics (*śramaṇas*).
Among them, those who are able to uphold the torch of wisdom and erect the banner of the Dharma are few.
To provide instruction that benefits others in the present moment and establishes a bridge for future generations—
is this not what I mean by "teaching"?
Thus, it is able to cause the two divisions of the Vinaya discipline to exert themselves with diligence without weariness, ensuring that their footsteps follow one another in succession without end.
The method of the Poṣadha washes away the cage of afflictions.
The merit of this abiding sustenance illuminates all moving and stationary beings.
I only pray that by means of these boundless causes of fortune, you may first employ them to adorn the Brahmā,
Śakra, the Four Heavenly Kings, and the eight classes of dragon and celestial beings.
May their merit and virtue increase ever further and their majestic radiance grow more intense;
may pestilence be eliminated and all living beings be benefited and brought joy;
and may the three borders be free from the anxieties of portents and calamities.
The hundred grains have attained the joy of abundant harvests.
Furthermore, we dedicate these merits to support the holy and divine Btsan-po.
We humbly pray that his brilliance may equal the realm of Shun and that he may harmonize with the virtues of Yao and Tang.
He bestows grace upon the eight directions and treats all sentient beings as his only child;
next, he employs merit to adorn my son, the *Jie'er Shanglun*.
I humbly pray that his glory may surpass those of past years and that his auspiciousness may increase on this present day.
This is intended to adorn the Duke She, the Commander-in-Chief;
may his blessings grow with each passing year and his longevity exceed that of metal and stone.
Thereafter, it is scattered and moistened throughout the Dharma-realm, reaching all sentient beings.
[End of the Text for the Four Seasons]. Indeed, when the Buddha-sun extends its radiance, there is no calamity that is not dispelled;
when Prajñā flows forth, blessings do not fail to arrive.
Now, the precious treasury of the eight dragons is opened;
the true texts of the five seals are revealed;
and the Dharma wheels of the two hundred [sutras] are assembled.
As for those who recite and chant this over a period of thirty days,
I shall now provide divine protection and blessing;
may the beginning of their meritorious virtues be set forth.
I humbly submit that the Way of Your Majesty, the Divine and Holy Emperor, surpasses that of Yi and Xuan;

your merit exceeds that of Yao and Shun. Grasping the charts and governing the calendar, you uphold the records and rectify the age; the eight directions are cleared and pacified, and your vast influence is widely propagated.
The family of the Ten Good Deeds, desiring to separately honor the sublime merit and uniquely establish a fragrant legacy,
constructed a four-season *dharmaparyāya* hall,
hoping that its influence upon myriad beings would endure for all eternity.
Because of this, [the Master] illuminated the deficiencies of his own practice; consequently, in Dunhuang today, the annual observance is maintained as a constant precept.
This year’s assembly concludes at the end of spring.
On this day, the fields are no longer green and the peach groves have ceased their crimson bloom.
The jade-colored robes face their end and the golden words of the decree are concluded.
Contemplating this extraordinary and boundless merit.
Consequently, he first employed these as adornments.
Indeed, his manifestations are boundless and his divine efficacy is tireless;
his grace extends to all things animate and inanimate.
Blessings permeate all living beings;
the God among Gods alone excels in his divine tasks.
As for such wondrous matters, what need is there for prolixity?
The arising of this auspicious omen surely has its cause.
Now, as the three months of spring are governed by their laws and the four seasons begin to divide,
the silk-like buds burst forth upon the southern branches.
The ice has melted at the northern bank.
I hope to broaden the traces of the Dharma King’s transformation so as to extend them beyond a thousand calamities,
and to propagate the glory of the Great Sage’s words so that ten thousand virtues may be attained.
Thereupon, they did not confine themselves to the Moon Palace;
at night, they struck the frost-bell and gathered the assembly of monastics.
Competing to hold up banners and canopies, they formed a magnificent assembly at the four gates and circled the capital city of the entire prefecture.
The golden countenance is established in an image;
though the clouds are not those of Vulture Peak,
the moonlight of the ūrṇā-hair shines from his brow.
The Lotus Palace of Flower Steps eclipsed the markets and cities,
shaking the mountains and surging through the valleys.
Having grown weary of desire in Kapilavastu, how could he have been bound by years?
It is my hope that the Four Kings who Guard the World, endowed with a hundred merits,
will secretly exert their power so that the *chancheng* (comets) shall be swept away at the gates of heaven,
and pestilence shall be hidden within the portals of the earth.
Auspicious clouds manifest the virtuous colors of the age;
they gather in the void and turn weapons upside down,
as culture is cultivated and martial force is laid to rest.
I dedicate all these merits to the eight classes of celestial beings, including the dragons and devas.
May their majestic radiance forever blaze and their spiritual powers be boundless;
may calamities not arise and disasters and chaos not occur.
Furthermore, by holding fast to these supreme merits, may they serve as superior provisions for the holy and divine btsan-po.
May it be prayed that the myriad nations submit tribute and the four seas come to court,
and that the precious reign endure forever in prosperity.
May his longevity be as enduring as metal and stone.
Furthermore, may he uphold supreme merit to adorn his son, the Regional Commander (Dudu).
We pray only that his life-span extend ever further and his emoluments reach ten thousand zhong, throughout all his tribes.
Let the officials at the Liaomen Gate pass on the nine halberds;
thereafter, may [the merit] be scattered and moistened throughout the Dharma-realm, universally reaching all sentient beings.
Relying upon this supreme cause, may all ascend to the fruits of bliss.
The account of the journey through the city is profound; how great is the beneficial manifestation of our Dharma King!
Thus, he descended his spirit from Tuṣita and manifested his form in the Royal City, observing that exquisite beauty is fraught with suffering, like a festering ulcer.
His jeweled remains abide beyond the imperial palaces;
he has subdued the four maras and ascended to perfect enlightenment,
dwelling within the three realms while alone claiming the title of Honored One.
The divine transformations are immeasurable and beyond the power of words to describe.
Now, in this month of spring’s warmth, the earth cracks open as sprouts emerge;
birds call out imbued with the springtime, and the wind sways.
Thus, the Nanda Garden was opened wide and the Lotus Palace was revealed;
the golden countenance shone brilliantly upon the four crossroads,
and the silver brow-hair radiated its light across the eight directions.
Mysteriously resounding and vast, it was like a city of white rice turning;
towering and majestic, it resembled the palaces of Kapilavastu encircled.
Those of high and low status flocked together, and the great and small rushed there like clouds.
As the lutes and songs compete in performance, they linger amidst the Dharma melodies;
as various offerings are presented, may the hopes of the assembly be fulfilled so that a hundred blessings may cover all.
May the thousand obstacles be dispelled like clouds, and by beholding this sublime form, may the cause for liberation be attained.
Beholding this wondrous form brings forth merit;
may all these manifold virtues result in no limited auspicious conditions.
First, one should offer adornments,
praying that Śakra, Brahmā, the Four Heavenly Kings,
and the eight classes of nāgas and devas will increase their majestic power and benefit their supernatural faculties.
Furthermore, may the miasmic vapors and pestilences be driven away;
next, may these supreme merits be employed for adornment by me,
the present holy and divine Btsan-po.
I humbly pray that Your Majesty’s life may be eternal and firm as heaven and earth, and that Your Virtue may command the six directions and encompass the four seas.

Furthermore, I pray that you will employ the Master Zhuangyan to discourse upon the Way, and that the Du Gong, the Regional Inspector, may act as clouds and rain to relieve all that is parched and withered.
In the morning, he dispatched various officials among the tribes to establish loyalty and integrity toward the holy campaign.
Thereafter, ascending into the void of the ultimate emptiness and extending throughout the ten directions,
he relied upon these supreme causes to attain the path of perfect enlightenment.
The patterns of his conduct and the inscriptions on the city walls reveal that his transformative manifestations are inexhaustible and his activities tireless.
His grace moistens all things animate and inanimate, and his blessings permeate all living beings.
Among those who dwell in heaven, he alone possesses supreme majesty.
As for these wondrous events, how could they be fully described with elaborate words?
There must surely be a profound reason for the auspicious signs of this assembly.
Now, as the four seasons are drawing to a close, [the time has come].
As the three months of spring have begun,
we bid farewell to the old and welcome the new;
we eliminate calamities and establish blessings.
I hope to purify the fortified borders and protect the common people.
Thereupon, at the moon palace, the frost-bell was struck through the night;
gathering the assembly of black-robed monks, they assembled there.
Everyone sought out banners and flowers to bring forth the Buddha image;

they circumambulated the layered city walls four times at the four gates. His majestic marks and signs were so solemn and sublime that even the clouds over Vulture Peak could not compare to their brilliance.

A ray of light from his brow shone like a lotus peak as he descended his steps; the entire city and marketplace were moved, shaking the valleys and rocking the mountains. Was it necessary to wait for years to see such a departure from the city at Śrāvastī?
I thus hope that the Four Heavenly Kings who protect the world will secretly bestow their hundredfold blessings,
so that the *chānqiāng* comet shall sweep away the gates of heaven and pestilence shall hide within the portals of the earth;
may the clouds spread forth and the multitude’s joyful countenances fill the void.
We lay down our weapons of war and cultivate culture to suppress militarism.
We dedicate all these merits to the eight classes of dragon and celestial beings,
praying that their majestic radiance shall forever blaze and their spiritual powers remain boundless.
May calamities not arise and disasters not occur.
Furthermore, may this sustained auspicious fortune be offered upward to support the divine and sagacious bTsan-po.
We pray only that the myriad nations may present tribute and the four seas may come to court.
May the precious reign endure forever, with longevity as enduring as metal and stone.
May the thunder of the Imperial Heir’s domain resound afar and the vast sea remain eternally serene;
may Lady Fu-ren-lan-gui be ever fragrant like the orchid and cassia.
The consorts and palace ladies offered hymns with divine flowers.
Furthermore, they took all their supreme merits to adorn our Duke Du, the Regional Commander, whose emolument reached ten thousand zhong.
Thereafter...
The Scripture for Recitation When on Military Campaign. Now, when the Buddhas give rise to compassion, it is universally prepared without conditions for all sentient beings.
Seeing their various manifestations and traces, they respond to causes; because they cause those who turn toward them to do so, blessings follow.
May those who harbor contempt and disparagement know that calamity arises following their own minds;
thus one knows that fortune and misfortune are brought about by oneself, and are not bestowed by the love or hatred of the Sage.
Now, the intent of this assembly’s recitation of the sutra is as follows:
Thus, I, the Minister of State of the Eastern Army, respectfully undertake this western expedition.
This is undertaken by me, the Retired Official Bao, as a meritorious act of cultivation.
I humbly beseech you, O Minister, whose brilliance was bestowed from Heaven and whose refined essence was nurtured by the Earth.
Mount Yue served as a bulwark for strategic defense, with plans devised through deliberation at the council table.
Yet, whenever the northern forces displayed their valor and raised armies to repeatedly violate the borders,
they plundered people and livestock and ravaged the fields and young crops.
The man’s countenance was unsettled like a mountain peak buffeted by frequent gusts of wind;
my countryman remained haughty, yet anger arose within him until his fury made his hair stand erect upon his head.
He then selected men of superior talent to lead the army on the western campaign;
although his strategic deliberations were as clear as looking at one's palm,
not even one in a hundred was left unaccounted for.
Nevertheless, one must certainly rely on the support of merit to ensure purity and auspiciousness. For this reason,
I have sent far-reaching greetings to my companions at Sanwei and offered prayers from afar for the texts of the Eight Treasuries,
hoping that our horses may remain safe and sound, and that our families and nations may enjoy eternal peace.
Therefore, I have caused those of reverent single-mindedness to chant the *Vajracchedikā*,
and the assembly of monks and nuns to proclaim the *Prajñāpāramitā*.
When one contemplates this extraordinary excellence, what could possibly surpass it?
First, I invoke the majestic and protective Four Heavenly Kings, the Nāgas, and the eight classes of deities,
praying that their radiant power and meritorious strength may increase,
so that the Western Chen and Qi will be brought into submission and the Northern Rong will be humbled and pay homage.
Furthermore, may these be used to adorn the generals and ministers of the military;
we pray that their wisdom and talent may flourish daily, their blessings accumulate like mountains,
and their lives endure for a long time as they preside over the steps of the throne.
May all those who serve [the Buddha], protected by the Three Jewels, adorn themselves with myriad virtues.
Thereafter,
as for the turning of the sūtra text— this manifestation of my Dharma King’s benefit is difficult to describe in detail.
Those who take refuge in it will surely achieve their fruits without fail.
Now, as for this opening of the Dragon Treasury, concentrating the mind to strike the great bell and inviting the two assemblies—
who has bestowed these upon us?
Thus, our country’s State Councilor, Chelpu-gyeong, established this as a merit for the protection of those who serve in the western expedition.
We humbly reflect that the State Councilor is a descent of the spirit of Mount He; his divine majesty moves all things, and he bestows universal grace.
On Departing the Frontier: To pacify the customs and stabilize the borders.
Just yesterday, at the beginning of spring, we raised the banners and prepared the boats for men and beasts.
From this, the military forces were mobilized on a grand scale to eliminate the wicked and the foul.
Although the army is strong and the officials are valiant,
blessings are but the teachers of calamity;
therefore, one should distance oneself from weapons in the shifting sands and offer earnest prayers with focused recitation.
Now that these meritorious deeds have been extensively arrayed and this supreme blessing is perfected,
it is used in its entirety to adorn the person of the General and Ministers of the Military.
We pray that all Buddhas will protect and mind them, so that there may be no cause for concern regarding injury or harm.
May the Eight Classes of Beings secretly bestow their vows to give rise to a spirit of descending harmony.
Thereafter, may both men and horses be entirely auspicious, and officials and soldiers be preserved in health.
May each maintain this state eternally, and may all warfare be abolished.
Thereafter, scatter [the remains] to moisten the entire *dharmadhātu*, reaching all sentient beings.
By relying on this, may they all together ascend the path of enlightenment.

Regarding the ritual for placing the parasol, the ritual for placing the parasol: indeed, there is nothing more effective than the secret mantra of the Buddha’s Uṣṇīṣa for dispelling calamities and pacifying hardships.
To accumulate merit and prolong blessings, one must rely on the practice of reciting mantras within the city of the mind.
Now that the spring sun has arrived, though the cold still holds its power this month,
I request that monks and nuns of the two divisions be invited to erect white banners at five locations.
Who was it that bestowed this?
At that time, it was established by Du Dushi, the Military Commissioner of Jie, as an act of merit to fulfill the vows for the sake of the common people of the entire district.
We humbly reflect that Military Commissioner Du Jie has governed all things with impartiality and exhausted his devotion to securing the borders.
Fearing that diseases may be cured [only to recur] and calamities may arise in succession,
one therefore cultivates great vows in advance to establish wholesome causes.
This is like building a city to extinguish the miasma of demonic vapors.
By erecting this banner, one attains the ultimate benefit and merit;
now that the ritual has been completed and the supreme vow fulfilled,
the resulting blessings are as vast as space, beyond all comparison.
With this victory, first adorn the Brahmās, Śakras, the Four Kings, and the eight classes of nāgas and spirits.
As for the inscription on the parasol, those who perceive its form and give rise to wholesome thoughts do so because it is none other than the body of an emanation.
In dispelling calamities and averting misfortunes, nothing surpasses the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī.
Thus, though it is a bodyless body, it manifests a form to equalize all hardships;
though it is beyond speech, it speaks to recite the heart-mantra and sustain those in peril.
No great occasion for prosperity has ever arisen greater than this.
Now, within the precincts of the Dunhuang Prefecture, the victorious banner of the White Dharma is erected;
the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa is installed at the four gates.
To cause the eradication of black karma—
now, who among those present in this assembly shall bestow it?
At that time, there were two youths, the provincial governor Du Gong and others.
This was established by Wei Chenghuang as a report for the sake of peace.
Only Jie'er Dushi considered that since the western frontier of Dunhuang borders the northern Hu,
those who gallop on horseback and draw their bowstrings— bandits and thieves— are unpredictable.
Fearing that [wild animals] might trample the crops and thereby diminish the source of food and clothing by ninety percent,
and that the nine types of agriculture failing to yield would cause the myriad people to ruin their hopes for suspended [provisions],
they devised mutual strategies with the sole aim of securing the peace of the people.
If one discusses protecting the state and rectifying the realm,
nothing surpasses erecting this banner and parasol;
it is precisely with the hope of eliminating calamities and misfortunes even in barren lands.
May pestilence be consigned to the realm of non-existence;
may the five grains be spared the calamities of frost and hail;
and may all things ascend to the city of human longevity.
Relying first upon this merit, we offer it to adorn and praise the Sage and the Divine.
We humbly pray that the precious throne may remain eternally firm, with a longevity as enduring as metal and stone;
that the four seas may be tranquil and clear, and that the myriad regions shall bring tribute to court.
He also maintained this virtuous and magnificent leadership as a commander-in-chief, acting as frost and rain to relieve drought and wither.
Thus, he caused the various officials of the Ming Chao tribes to establish loyalty and integrity within the sagely era.
Furthermore, may this virtue also serve as an adornment for my two preceptors who provide instruction.
I pray that they may utterly uproot all extraordinary suffering and transcend the cycle of saṃsāra.
May your lifespan be as enduring as the cold pine and your blessings as abundant as spring grass.
Thereafter, may these benefits lightly moisten all animate and inanimate beings throughout the boundless reaches.
Relying upon this supreme cause, may we ascend the path to Perfect Enlightenment.
The Inscription for the Parasol: Now, the extension of auspiciousness and the unfolding of celebration must rely upon the victorious banner;
the sweeping away of sprouts of misfortune and the elimination of calamities require the power of the child.
Thus, it was made so that Shan-zhu (Susthitamati) might hear of his increased longevity.
Ānanda realized his original mind;
the *chi-mei* spirits feared him and fled from punishment;
the celestial Māra was terrified and sought salvation.
How great is the divine child!
Truly beyond all words of praise.
Now, as the gentle spring breeze stirs all creatures and the doors of hibernation open.
As the banners and canopies were being unfurled, the assembly of monastics stood in solemn reverie;
what was the reason for this? It was because at that time, there was my disciple Jie'er, who, together with the Prefect Du Gong and others, engaged in a profound discussion.
Furthermore, he nurtured the people as if they were his own children and regarded the state's affairs with the same concern as his own family.
Fearing that demonic vapors would run rampant within the city and that all living beings would repeatedly suffer the calamities of rebellion, [he acted].
Therefore, in this month of the three yangs, we open the three blessings for the World-Honored One Śākyamuni;
at the first hour of the four seasons, we establish the benefits of the four gates.
We encompass all these extraordinary and wondrous, most supreme fields of merit.
May all the Brahmā, Śakra, the Four Heavenly Kings, nāgas, and the eight classes of spirits be fully adorned and honored.
We pray that their majestic radiance and the power of their abundant blessings may increase,
so that they may nurture the common people and protect the army and the state.
I, the holy and divine Emperor,
pray only that your sacred person may remain firm and long-lived as the days pass and the months come.
May the precious dwelling endure forever and ever;
may Heaven be long-lasting and Earth eternal.
May the Duke, Son of Heaven, live as long as the mountains and rivers.
May blessings and auspiciousness mutually support one another.
We, the tribal chieftains and various officials,
pray only that you will assist us in maintaining peace and harmony.
Only when purity and uprightness prevail will the four seasons proceed in harmony, the five grains flourish,
a hundred calamities be eliminated, and ten thousand auspicious signs gather.
The Prajñā deity-child is the teacher of all Buddhas;
the great assembly recites it everywhere throughout the city.
